name: Hope Shaman Spirit
body:
A shaman who selects the hope spirit has a calming demeanor and you feel comfortable in their presence.

Spirit Magic Spells: lesser good hope (1st), encouragement (2nd), good hope (3rd), greater path of glory (4th), shining beacon (5th), greater good hope (6th), hymn of peace (7th), euphoric tranquility (8th), beacon of life (9th)

Hexes: A shaman who chooses the hope spirit can select from the following hexes.

Calming Words (Ex)

You gain a +4 bonus on Diplomacy checks to alleviate despair (see the New Skill Uses section on page 43) or improve disposition.

You may alleviate despair on two targets in a single standard action. Additionally you may use Diplomacy to alleviate despair on yourself.

Guard Resolve (Ex)

With a touch, you can provide a +4 bonus on saving throws against fear and despair effects and the DC to use Intimidation to demoralize or induce despair (See New Skill Uses on page 43) in the target is increased by 4.

Keeper of Hope (Su)

As a move action, you can call upon an inner reserve of resolve. You gain a +1 morale bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls, and Will saves against fear and despair for a number of rounds equal to your Charisma bonus. At 7th level, this bonus increases to +2, and at 14th level this bonus increases to +3. You can only benefit from this hex once per 24 hours.

Touch of Hope (Su)

As a standard action, you can perform a melee touch attack that can ease the targets fears and doubts. If the target is affected by a fear or despair condition, the condition is removed. Once affected by this hex, the creature cannot be the target of this hex again for 24 hours.

Spirit Animal: The shaman’s spirit animal is glorious and you are inspired just by being around it. It gains a +4 bonus on Will saves vs. fear and despair.

Spirit Ability: A shaman who chooses the hope spirit as their spirit or wandering spirit gains the following ability.

Channel (Su)

You can channel positive energy like a cleric, using your oracle level as your effective cleric level when determining the amount of damage healed. This channeling cannot be used to harm undead. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier.

Greater Spirit Ability: A shaman who chooses the hope spirit as their spirit or wandering spirit gains the following ability upon having access to the greater version of that spirit.

Rallying Cry (Ex)

As a standard action, you can let out a rallying cry. All allies within 100 feet that can hear your call gain the benefits of lesser heroism for a number of rounds equal to your Charisma modifier. At 10th level, this increases to heroism. You can use this ability once per day, plus one additional time per day at 5th level and for every five levels thereafter.

True Spirit Ability: A shaman who chooses the hope spirit as their spirit or wandering spirit gains the following ability upon having access to the true version of that spirit.

Healing Hopes (Su)

When you cast a spell with the hope descriptor you may heal one of the affected spell targets per 5 levels (minimum 1). The healing is equal to 1d8 plus the morale bonus provided for spells up to 3rd level, 2d8 plus the morale bonus provided for spells from 4th to 6th level, and 3d8 plus the morale bonus for spells from 7th to 9th levels. This healing does not affect non-living creatures but it does not harm undead.

You can use this ability once per day, plus one additional time per day at 5th level, and every five levels thereafter.

Manifestation: At 20th level, you become a living beacon of hope exuding an aura of hope out to 30 feet.

Any spell with the despair descriptor cast within the aura requires a concentration check as if the caster was defensively casting. Any spell with the hope descriptor cast within the aura is automatically extended per the metamagic feat without increasing the spell level. This extension does not stack with an application of the metamagic feat. Finally, each round you may dispel any despair effect within the aura as per the spell dispel magic as a free action.
